title: What can you do on the tee?
question: Which of these actions are allowed on the teeing area before your first shot? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Evening out uneven ground for a better stance.
Pulling up loose grass that might affect your shot.
Moving the tee-markers to change your starting spot.

explanation: You can prepare the surface by smoothing the ground and removing natural loose items like grass or twigs, but must never move the tee-markers.

juniorVersion.title: What are you allowed to do on the teeing area?
juniorVersion.question: Before you hit your first shot, which things can you do on the teeing area? Choose all the ones you are allowed to do.

choices.text: Make the ground flat with your foot so you can stand better.
Pull out loose bits of grass that might be in your way.
Pick up stones or sticks that are not stuck in the ground.
Move the tee-markers to pick a different place to hit from.

juniorVersion.explanation: On the teeing area, you can fix the ground to stand better and take away loose grass, stones or sticks. But you must never move the tee-markers.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The place where you start a hole. It is between two markers and goes back a bit.
Coloured blocks that show where you must hit your first shot from.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids the teeing area on the course and let them practise clearing loose bits and checking the tee-markers.
likelyMisconceptions: Some may think moving the tee-markers is allowed.
Some may think you can't touch anything on the ground.
